self: The name was their own, used at gatherings and in the recitation of descent.
They called themselves this long before anyone wrote it down.
Elders taught the name to children as the first thing they should know about who they were.
neighbour.respectful: Their neighbours coined the name out of respect for {custom}.
Those who traded with them named them for {feature}, and meant it kindly.
neighbour.neutral: Communities nearby first used the name for the people of the {feature}.
Travellers gave them the name because it was the plainest way to say where they lived.
neighbour.hostile: Rivals coined the name as a jibe at {custom}.
It began as an insult shouted across a disputed border.
geographical: The name began as a plain description of the settlements around the {feature}.
It named the country first and the people second.
dynastic: The ruling house traced its line to {ancestor}, and the name proclaimed it.
The name was taken by the heirs of {ancestor} to set them above other families.
ceremonial: The title was spoken at councils and in war-songs, never in ordinary speech.
Priests and singers used the name; most people used something plainer.
later: Chroniclers applied the name to several communities they could not tell apart.
Map-makers wrote the name across a region they knew only from report.
imposed: Imperial officials recorded the name when the region was brought under tribute.
Conquerors used the name in their tax rolls, and it stuck.

meaning.landscape: It refers to the {feature} at the heart of their lands.
meaning.water: It recalls the {feature} on which their lives depended.
meaning.warfare: It boasts of {emblem} and the battles fought with it.
meaning.plants: The {plant} stood at the centre of their oldest settlement.
meaning.sacred: It names the {sacred} they held holy.
meaning.number: It counts {number} groups bound together by oath.
meaning.lifeway: It names the work that fed them: they were {lifeway}.
meaning.speech: It turns on how they spoke, which was the first thing strangers noticed.
meaning.dress: It describes how they looked to others: {dress}.
meaning.vessel: It remembers {vessel}, which first brought them to this land.
meaning.relationship: It sets them in relation to the centre of the known world.

qualityGloss.High: the people of the high ground
qualityGloss.Watchful: a watchful people, slow to trust
qualityGloss.Free: a free people, subject to no one

directionGloss.Upper Half: in the upper half of a divided people
directionGloss.Lower Half: in the lower half of a divided people
directionGloss.Left-Hand: on the left hand of the ruler
directionGloss.Right-Hand: on the right hand of the ruler

acceptance.embraced: They took the name as their own and use it with pride.
acceptance.accepted: They accepted the name without complaint.
acceptance.tolerated: They tolerated the name but rarely used it among themselves.
acceptance.resented: They resented the name and corrected anyone who used it.
acceptance.reclaimed: Later generations took up the insult and wore it with pride.
acceptance.unknown: Whether they ever used the name themselves is not recorded.

drift.broadened: In time it came to cover the whole of the surrounding region.
drift.narrowed: In time it came to mean only the ruling families.
drift.passed to the land: The land itself now bears the name.
drift.outlived: The name has outlived the people it once described.
drift.transferred: The people who replaced them took the name over.
drift.became a title: It survives as a title rather than the name of a people.

interpretations.text: sacred animal, which they must never harm or eat

history.transplanted: Their ancestors brought the old ways of naming with them into {biome}.
history.echo: The name echoes that of a real historical people.
